# Chat spike phrases. One per line: "<phrase> | <expected outcome>".
# Expected outcome is one of: proposal, plain, invalid. Lines starting with # are ignored.
# Categories available to the model: Rent, Phone, Subscriptions (fixed); Groceries, Entertainment, Transport (flexible); Salary (income).

# --- 10 clean and typical (expect a confident proposal) ---
today I spent 10 on groceries | proposal
spent 4.50 on transport | proposal
rent is 190 | proposal
add income 2000 salary | proposal
paid 35 for phone yesterday | proposal
set groceries weekly target to 80 | proposal
delete the last transaction | proposal
what's my balance | proposal
spent 25 on entertainment today | proposal
subscriptions 12 today | proposal

# --- 10 with typos and abbreviations (expect a proposal) ---
spnt 7.75 on grocries | proposal
transprt 3.20 today | proposal
pd rent 190 | proposal
set grocery wkly tgt 90 | proposal
del last txn | proposal
phone bill 35 nxt mon | proposal
incm 100 salary | proposal
entertanment 9.80 | proposal
groceris 12 | proposal
coffee 2.50 at hofer | question

# --- 5 reworded or indirect (expect a proposal) ---
I grabbed some transport for 2 euros | proposal
put down 15 for groceries | proposal
move my weekly groceries budget to 100 | proposal
that last one was actually 20 | proposal
scratch the last entry | proposal

# --- 5 vague (should NOT produce a confident proposal) ---
the usual | plain
money stuff | plain
hmm not sure | plain
help | plain
what can you do | plain

# --- arithmetic / relative amounts, BOTH kinds (PENDING the owner's local run — see spike-results.md) ---
# Arithmetic is decided in code and runs BEFORE the model, so these never depend on the model proposing an
# action (it returns "none" for bare phrases). Expected values are what the code must produce.
#
# Bare arithmetic (no target named) → the which-target question "€X for which target?". "that"/"it" refer to
# the last amount earlier in the thread, so the reference phrases assume a prior message established it.
divide that by 4 | question                          # (ref 80) expect "€20.00 for which target?", working "80 ÷ 4 = 20"
half of that | question                              # (ref 60) expect "€30.00 for which target?", working "half of 60 = 30"
double it | question                                 # (ref 15) expect "€30.00 for which target?", working "double 15 = 30"
10% of 250 | question                                # expect "€25.00 for which target?", working "10% of 250 = 25"
#
# Arithmetic that names a target → a set_budget_target proposal with the working appended.
set groceries weekly target to divide 80 by 4 | proposal   # expect "Set Groceries weekly target to €20.00 (now €0.00) (80 ÷ 4 = 20)"
set groceries monthly target to half of 80 | proposal      # expect "Set Groceries monthly target to €40.00 (now €0.00) (half of 80 = 40)"
set groceries weekly target to 10% of 250 | proposal       # expect "Set Groceries weekly target to €25.00 (now €0.00) (10% of 250 = 25)"
#
split 60 between 3 | invalid                         # expect the share-or-total question, no proposal
